input.rationale: Repaired a knowledge mislabel from the previous turn. The correction that added the post-shutdown evidence was submitted against the stall-route entry (983e6d23976b4e4e9eff6a3987874db1-knowledge-0) instead of the shutdown entry (c27ce810268e4535bf01c8870a682db4-knowledge-0), so the stall Fact was overwritten by the shutdown premise. This update restores the stall premise under its own id with the wording of its revision 1 and re-points its execution at the stall receipt, and it applies the intended refinement to the shutdown entry under its own id: the operative condition is the buffered verifyCh plus a future without ShutdownCh rather than the timing of the shutdown. Both entries now describe their own behaviour, both changed premises are recorded, and no measurement is withdrawn.

knowledge.statement: A VerifyLeader request queued while a leader's main loop is stalled past its lease is answered without success once the stall ends, even though a successor has been elected in the meantime. Across eight trials the stalled leader held only Leader state for every 1ms sample while another server led at term 3 (first seen at 345-464ms), yet the queued verify returned non-nil in all eight: seven times 'leadership lost while committing log' and twice 'node is not the leader', at 600-602ms, the moment the stall released the main loop; the concurrent Apply failed the same way. The endpoints show the lease case was already ready when the loop resumed, so leadership was given up before the non-voter's acknowledgement could be counted, which is ordering rather than the eligibility rule that the verify quorum itself violates.
knowledge.conditions: Three voters plus one non-voter, the leader partitioned so only the non-voter is reachable, HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 200ms, a 600ms stall that blocks StoreLogs on the leader's main thread while a client Apply is in flight, in-memory transports in one process.
knowledge.changed_premise: The premise is restored, not changed: revision 2 of this entry recorded the shutdown-strand premise, which belongs to c27ce810268e4535bf01c8870a682db4-knowledge-0, so this revision re-states the stall-route premise of revision 1 and re-points the executions at that receipt.

knowledge.statement: VerifyLeader can hand back a future that nothing will ever complete, because the request waits in the buffered verifyCh that no reader drains once the run loop has exited and the future itself carries no shutdown channel to unblock on. The trigger does not require racing Shutdown: calls made after Shutdown has already returned strand about half the time, since the closed shutdown channel and a send into the 64-slot verifyCh are both selectable. In the revision, post-shutdown VerifyLeader calls were answered 4, 3 and 3 of 8 times and left unanswered 4, 5 and 5 times (14 of 24 stranded), while Barrier and Apply answered all 48 of their post-shutdown calls with ErrRaftShutdown, which matches verifyCh being buffered and applyCh unbuffered by default. The earlier receipt shows the racing form as well, leaving 9 and 41 of 64 futures incomplete in two of three trials with none in the control.
knowledge.conditions: Single-voter Raft instance, HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 50ms, in-memory transport in one process, BatchApplyCh not set; 64 concurrent calls issued just before Shutdown in the first receipt and 128 with an interleaved shutdown plus 8 post-shutdown calls in the revision.
knowledge.changed_premise: The trigger is corrected rather than extended: the behaviour was first described as a VerifyLeader call handed back while Shutdown is in progress, and the revision shows the same strand for calls issued after Shutdown has already returned, so the operative condition is the buffered verifyCh with no drainer and a future without ShutdownCh, not the timing of the shutdown. The racing evidence of the first receipt is kept and the post-shutdown counts are added.

knowledge.statement: VerifyLeader counts acknowledgements from non-voters toward a voter-sized quorum, so it can report success for an interval in which the leader has had no successful interaction with any other voter. verifyLeader registers every entry of leaderState.replState (which startStopReplication creates for every configured server except the leader itself, without consulting Suffrage) on repl.notify, so each of those peers is asked to acknowledge; a successful AppendEntries reply (updateLastAppended and the heartbeat path) or a successful InstallSnapshot replies with notifyAll(true), which calls verifyFuture.vote(true) and increments votes; the threshold compared against is quorumSize(), computed as (voters in configurations.latest)/2+1. Every other leadership-quorum test in the same package restricts eligibility to voters: checkLeaderLease skips non-voter servers in its contacted count and requestVote rejects a candidate without a vote, so the two leadership tests disagree about whose support counts.
knowledge.conditions: A leader whose latest configuration (configurations.latest) contains a server with Suffrage other than Voter, and which can still exchange AppendEntries or InstallSnapshot RPCs with that server. With three voters and one non-voter, quorumSize() is 2, so the leader's own vote plus one non-voter acknowledgement reaches the threshold.

knowledge.statement: The leader's own leadership lease is computed over voters only: checkLeaderLease counts itself plus those servers in configurations.latest whose Suffrage is Voter and whose followerReplication last contact is within LeaderLeaseTimeout, and steps down when that count is below quorumSize(). A leader therefore stops counting an unreachable voter as contacted and steps down within roughly LeaderLeaseTimeout of the last successful interaction, while a follower cannot campaign before ElectionTimeout has elapsed since it last heard from a leader.
knowledge.conditions: A configuration accepted by Config.Validate, which requires 5ms <= LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout <= ElectionTimeout; the lease check is driven by the leader's own timer and by the last-contact times its replication goroutines record.

knowledge.statement: Runtime configuration reload enforces the same timeout bounds as initial construction: ReloadConfig applies the reloadable fields onto the current configuration and returns the error from ValidateConfig before storing it, so LeaderLeaseTimeout can never exceed HeartbeatTimeout, nor HeartbeatTimeout exceed ElectionTimeout, on a running node. A leader cannot therefore be given a longer lease than a follower's election timeout through the public reload API.
knowledge.conditions: A call to Raft.ReloadConfig on a running node with a protocol-supported configuration; the check is performed under r.confReloadMu before the new configuration is stored, and on failure the previous configuration remains in force.

knowledge.statement: LeadershipTransferToServer accepts a non-voter target and reports success without transferring leadership to it. The leader resolves the requested ID in leaderState.replState, which contains an entry for every configured server except the leader (startStopReplication creates one per server without consulting Suffrage) and only errors with 'cannot find replication state' when no entry exists. The selected target is sent TimeoutNow, which sets it to Candidate and marks candidateFromLeadershipTransfer; that flag makes runCandidate skip pre-vote, so the target sends a real RequestVote carrying the next term. A voter handling that request adopts the higher term and becomes a follower before it reaches the hasVote check, which then refuses the vote because the candidate holds no vote; the candidate therefore cannot win. When the old leader observes the higher term it steps down, the transfer goroutine's leftLeaderLoop branch responds nil, and the caller sees success. By contrast LeadershipTransfer with no explicit target picks through pickServer, which skips every server whose Suffrage is not Voter.
knowledge.conditions: Protocol version >= 3 (otherwise LeadershipTransferToServer returns ErrUnsupportedProtocol), a cluster whose latest configuration at the leader contains the named server with Suffrage other than Voter, and pre-vote enabled or disabled (the transfer path skips pre-vote either way). The named server must be reachable from the leader, otherwise the leader reports a TimeoutNow failure instead.

knowledge.statement: A leadership transfer requested for a non-voter leaves the cluster without a leader until a voter wins the next election, while the call itself has already reported success. In the observed run with HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 200ms, the call returned nil, the requested non-voter was never Leader, the previous leader was sampled outside Leader state in all 1289 samples from the instant of the call, 241 samples found no leader at all (first 1ms, last 278ms after the call, about 1.4 election timeouts), the maximum term rose from 2 to 4, and a different voter held leadership at the end. The voter-target control with the same call returned nil and did hand leadership to the requested server.
knowledge.conditions: Cluster of three voters plus one non-voter joined through AddNonvoter, protocol version >= 3, all peers reachable, pre-vote left at its default, and a single process with in-memory transports; the target is chosen by its suffrage in the leader's latest configuration, not by any observed result.

knowledge.statement: Election vote solicitation is restricted to voters, unlike the verify path in the same file. electSelf and preElectSelf both iterate configurations.latest.Servers and act only when server.Suffrage == Voter: the local server records a vote for itself and every other server is asked with a RequestVote or RequestPreVote RPC, while non-voters are skipped altogether, so no non-voter grant is ever counted toward the voter-sized quorum they compare against. The grant side is not what keeps non-voters out: requestVote rejects a candidate that holds no vote and a candidate that is not in the configuration, but it imposes no suffrage requirement on the server granting, and it persists and grants a vote whenever the candidate's log is at least as up to date, so a non-voter would grant if it were asked. verifyLeader is the path that does ask every entry of leaderState.replState, which includes non-voters.
knowledge.conditions: A server whose latest configuration contains non-voting members, with pre-vote either enabled (preElectSelf) or disabled (electSelf directly); the solicitation loops read configurations.latest on the candidate's own main thread.

knowledge.statement: A follower attempts an election after HeartbeatTimeout without contact from a leader, and ElectionTimeout governs only a candidate's retry. runFollower arms heartbeatTimer with randomTimeout(HeartbeatTimeout) and campaigns when the time since last contact is at least HeartbeatTimeout, while runCandidate arms its timer with randomTimeout(ElectionTimeout) and simply restarts the election when it fires. randomTimeout(v) returns v plus a random fraction of v, so a campaign begins in [H, 2H). Correspondingly ValidateConfig requires LeaderLeaseTimeout <= HeartbeatTimeout <= ElectionTimeout, and the leader's own lease check runs every max(minCheckInterval, LeaderLeaseTimeout - maxDiff) with minCheckInterval = 10ms, stepping down at the first check whose voter contact age exceeds LeaderLeaseTimeout; the comparison is diff <= leaseTimeout, so a check at exactly the boundary still counts the voter as contacted.
knowledge.conditions: The default follower and leader loops in this snapshot, with pre-vote enabled or disabled; the numbers quoted are for a configuration accepted by ValidateConfig, and the exposure analysis assumes in-memory or low-latency RPCs.
